voiceover: Did Jesus of Nazareth rise from the dead? Everything in Christianity stands or falls on the answer, so this section examines it as carefully as any claim in history. It begins with a handful of facts even sceptical scholars grant, and asks what best explains them — the minimal-facts approach. The core is not late. Paul hands on a creed the church was reciting within a few years of the crucifixion — not a legend that grew over lifetimes. The evidence points to an empty tomb; the appearances were too many and too varied to explain away as hallucinations. Frightened disciples became willing to suffer and die rather than deny what they said they saw. And men with every reason not to believe — Paul, who had persecuted the church, and James, Jesus's own sceptical brother — came to faith. Every one of these arguments gets a fully-cited deep-dive essay. Each claim is sourced, and the strongest objections are stated fairly, then answered. That is our standard — Checked Before Published. And you will not just read. On every essay an AI tutor answers your questions — ask it anything, or highlight a single sentence and ask about that exact line. Mastery mode lets you explain the argument back in your own words and have it graded. Daily practice brings the key points back just as you are about to forget them. There are pocket cards to share, and a Debate Arena to practise against an AI sceptic before the real conversation. Every essay comes in a plain-English version and a full deep dive, with read-aloud audio. History's own tools cannot compel faith, but they can weigh explanations — and the case here is that the best one is that he rose. Weigh it yourself. Start anywhere, and follow it where it leads.
